d.note: Family-owned New Hartford restaurant, bar and bakery; chicken riggies and its Utica-style 'Greens CaNole' are on the menu.
d.fn: The bakery says it has served Central New York for over two decades; opening year at Campion Rd not confirmed.

d.note: New Hartford bakery known for its half moon cookies.
Utica bagel bakery that makes its bagels from scratch with four ingredients, ferments them overnight, then kettles and bakes them every day.
d.fn: Its site says founder Ed Grove left GE during the 1980s bagel craze to start it and has refined the recipe for over 30 years. The year at this address isn't stated.

d.note: Italian restaurant in Utica known for its chicken riggies; also serves Utica greens.
North Genesee Street successor to the Chesterfield restaurant on Bleecker Street, with Utica greens and chicken riggies on the menu.
d.fn: Successor to Dominique's Chesterfield Restaurant at 1713 Bleecker St, run by a family long tied to chicken riggies and Utica greens; founding-year claims not confirmed.

d.note: Bleecker Street Italian pastry shop known for pusties, with half moons in the case too.
d.fn: Opened December 1928 at 605 Bleecker St; moved to 667 Bleecker St in 1945 (its site).

d.note: Utica bakery that calls its hand-frosted half moon 'the original', made to a 1920 recipe.
d.fn: The bakery says its half moon is 'the original' and that the recipe hasn't changed since 1920 (its claim); I LOVE NY also dates the cookie's debut at Hemstrought's to 1920.

d.note: Utica kitchen and bar built around the city's own dishes: riggies, Utica greens and tomato pie.
Utica Italian bakery named among the city's tomato pie stops.
Utica pizzeria dating to 1914 that began with nickel tomato pies; still family-run and known for its 'upside-down' sausage pie.
d.fn: Founded 1914 by Eugeno Burlino (the family name is also spelled Burline), who sold nickel tomato pies; year at 614 Bleecker St not confirmed.

d.note: Italian deli and sausage maker on Bleecker St known for its homemade tomato pie.
Utica bagel café known for custom-colored bagels. I LOVE NY (2025) says it recently opened a second Utica location.
Washington Mills branch of the Utica deli, selling the same tomato pie.
Westmoreland family farm market with a greenhouse and an in-house bakery that sells mini and jumbo half moon cookies.
d.fn: A family-run farm market and bakery since 1986 (its site).

d.note: Family bakery and deli known for half moons, jelly buns and Utica-style tomato pie, with a drive-up window.
d.fn: Holland Farms opened its first dairy bar and bakery in Yorkville in 1955 and moved to 50 Oriskany Blvd in 1966 (its history page).

d.note: Lakeside resort hotel on Otsego Lake whose dining rooms include the 1909 Restaurant and the Hawkeye Bar & Grill.
d.fn: Resort hotel open since 1909 (its claim); its steakhouse is named the 1909 Restaurant

d.note: Inn, restaurant and tavern in an 1802 building in the village of Cooperstown.
d.fn: Building dates to 1802 (built as the American Hotel per Wikipedia; other accounts say it was a store first and a hotel from 1848); named the Tunnicliff Inn since 1916
